rules.title: The page threw an error that nothing caught
rules.expected: The page runs without throwing an error that nothing handles.
rules.whyItMatters: An uncaught error usually means part of the page stopped working, often with no message to the user. It shows up as a button that does nothing or a blank section.
rules.fixHint: Fix the code that throws this error and handle the failure where it can happen, so the page shows a message instead of breaking.

rules.title: The page logged an error to the console
rules.expected: The browser console stays free of errors while the page loads and is used.
rules.whyItMatters: An error in the console is usually something that went wrong behind the scenes, such as a failed request, a broken component or a missing file. Users may not see the error, but they see its effects.
rules.fixHint: Find the code that logs this error and fix its cause, and remove the log line only once the cause is gone.

rules.title: The page logged a warning
rules.expected: The browser console stays free of warnings while the page loads and is used.
rules.whyItMatters: A warning is an early sign of trouble: something outdated, misused or about to break. It is cheap to fix now and costly to track down later.
rules.fixHint: Read the warning text, then change the code it points to so the warning no longer appears.

rules.title: A request the page made failed on the server
rules.expected: Every request the page makes is answered without a server error, that is, without a status of 500 or higher.
rules.whyItMatters: The server broke while handling the request, so the data or action the page asked for did not happen. Users see an empty list, a spinner that never ends or a save that silently fails.
rules.fixHint: Fix the server code behind this request so it stops failing, and make the page show a clear message when a request fails anyway.

rules.title: A request the page made was rejected
rules.expected: Every request the page makes is accepted by the server, with no rejection such as not found (404), not allowed (403) or bad request (400).
rules.whyItMatters: The page asked for something the server would not give: a file that is missing, a login that has lapsed, or data in the wrong shape. The feature that depended on it is likely broken.
rules.fixHint: Fix the URL, credentials or data this request sends so the server accepts it, or remove the request if it is no longer needed.

rules.title: A request the page made never got an answer
rules.expected: Every request the page makes gets an answer from a server.
rules.whyItMatters: The request never reached a server or never came back: the address is wrong, the server is down, or the browser blocked it. Whatever depended on the answer cannot work.
rules.fixHint: Fix the address or the server this request goes to, and show a message in the page when no answer comes back.

rules.title: A placeholder value leaked into the page
rules.expected: The page never shows internal placeholder values such as undefined, null, NaN or [object Object] as text.
rules.whyItMatters: These words appear when the app tried to show data it did not have, so visitors read something like Last edited by undefined. It looks careless and often hides a real bug.
rules.fixHint: Find where this text is built, make sure the value exists before it is shown, and show a sensible fallback or leave the label out when it does not.

rules.title: A translation key is shown instead of its text
rules.expected: The page shows readable text, not translation keys such as settings.timezone.hint.
rules.whyItMatters: A translation key on screen means the text is missing for this language, or the translation file did not load. Visitors see code instead of a sentence and cannot tell what the label means.
rules.fixHint: Add the missing entry for this key to the translation file for the current language, or fix how that file is loaded.

rules.title: A template placeholder was not filled in
rules.expected: The page never shows template placeholders such as {{name}} or {count} that were meant to be replaced with real values.
rules.whyItMatters: The app was supposed to fill in a name, a number or a date and did not. Visitors see raw template code, which looks unfinished and leaves out what they needed to know.
rules.fixHint: Pass the missing value into the template that renders this text, or fix the placeholder name so it matches the value you supply.
